derivation: Hand-transcribed recipes of work/lead/cp2a-owner-preparation/lease-draft.md applied to the frozen financial pages by cases/cp2a-owner/builder/build.py (stdlib only; deploy_vii never imported or run). Every value is the correctly rounded 38-significant-digit half-even quotient of an exact rational (Fraction), cross-checked against decimal.Context(prec=38, ROUND_HALF_EVEN); display spelling follows display.py (ROUND_HALF_UP; amount 2 dp by the fact's decimals, multiple 2 dp 'x', percent 1 dp '%', negative in parentheses). CP-1 constants are derived from the frozen pages and asserted against the financial oracle; only CP-1's value_class and cell text are observed strings.

cell_notation.shown: exact displayed text; an unsettled cell is spelled as report_view.fact_spelling spells it: missing -> state gap, text '∅ G#'; not_applicable -> state not_meaningful, text '∅ G# n.m.' (G# is the report-wide gap number, not literal)
cell_notation.amount_exact: canonical exact decimal; null means unsettled
cell_notation.derives_from: the CP-1 T4.10 metrics (cases.<case>.cp1_inputs keys) a calculated fact derives from; empty for analyst inputs and definition constants

id_rules.scenario_rows: s01.. in submission order; s00 is the Python base control
id_rules.break_rows: b01 fcf_zero, b02 coverage_floor, b03.. thresholds in submission order
id_rules.claims: T2B.1.sNN (scenario rationale), T2B.4.sNN, T2B.7.first, T2B.1.assessment, in this order
id_rules.cp1_references_rows: ref01.. : the CP-1 facts named by {{FIG}} references in the submission's prose in reading order (scenarios, thresholds, assessment, gaps), then the four reported ratios T2B.5 compares, each CP-1 fact once

lineage_rule: M2: a calculated fact's citations are the ordered, de-duplicated concatenation of the citations of the CP-1 facts in its derives_from list, in that order (cp4_legal._computed pattern: tuple(dict.fromkeys((*first, *second)))); its period is the base period; a known fact never derives from a CP-1 fact that is not known (asserted by the builder). A stressed FCF lists cash_interest only when the interest increase is non-zero.
cp1_references_rule: Each row carries the CP-1 fact verbatim under its own fact_id (bound at run time), with the CP-1 fact's own value_class, status and limitation; prose and T2B.5 reference it ({<CP-1 fact_id>|<unit>}). No CP-2A table or claim stores a spelled CP-1 figure.

property_tests.round_trip: M1: for every break point with a required decline s*, evaluating the stress recipe in fractions.Fraction over the Decimal inputs at the exact rational s* gives exactly the break level; there is no tolerance and no 38-digit rounding in the statement (a 38-digit Decimal s* fed back can miss the level by one unit in the last place; the builder asserts the Fraction form for every break of every case)
property_tests.base_control: stress with decline 0 and increase 0 equals the base ratios (s00)
property_tests.monotonic: stressed EBITDA, FCF and coverage do not rise, and leverage does not fall, as the decline rises (where calculable)

Under the Moderate downturn scenario, stressed EBITDA is {T2B.3.s01.ebitda|US$ m} against {T2B.3.s00.ebitda|US$ m} at base, free cash flow is {T2B.3.s01.fcf|US$ m}, net leverage is {T2B.4.s01.net_leverage|x} and interest coverage is {T2B.4.s01.interest_coverage|x}.

Under the Severe downturn scenario, stressed EBITDA is {T2B.3.s02.ebitda|US$ m} against {T2B.3.s00.ebitda|US$ m} at base, free cash flow is {T2B.3.s02.fcf|US$ m}, net leverage is {T2B.4.s02.net_leverage|x} and interest coverage is {T2B.4.s02.interest_coverage|x}.

Under the Severe downturn with higher rates scenario, stressed EBITDA is {T2B.3.s03.ebitda|US$ m} against {T2B.3.s00.ebitda|US$ m} at base, free cash flow is {T2B.3.s03.fcf|US$ m}, net leverage is {T2B.4.s03.net_leverage|x} and interest coverage is {T2B.4.s03.interest_coverage|x}.

Under the Total loss of earnings scenario, stressed EBITDA is {T2B.3.s04.ebitda|US$ m} against {T2B.3.s00.ebitda|US$ m} at base, free cash flow is {T2B.3.s04.fcf|US$ m}, net leverage is [T2B.4.s04.net_leverage] and interest coverage is {T2B.4.s04.interest_coverage|x}.
The first test reached is Free cash flow at or below zero at an EBITDA decline of {T2B.7.r01.required_decline|%}.

The credit starts from total leverage of {{FIG:total_leverage_reported|x}}, net leverage of {{FIG:net_leverage_reported|x}}, interest coverage of {{FIG:interest_coverage_reported|x}} and free cash flow of {{FIG:fcf_ltm|US$ m}}; the scenarios test how far earnings can fall before those measures reach the watch levels.

own_limitations: Scenario shock sizes are analyst assumptions without a source citation.
Break-point watch levels are analyst assumptions, not covenants; no covenant owner is an input.
Stress is applied to the base period's flows with debt and cash held at their reported closing balances; no forward cash build, refinancing or mitigating action is modelled.
Cash taxes, capital expenditure and working capital are held at the base period; no tax shield is taken.
Liquidity is not tested: stressed free cash flow is not set against the cash balance or any undrawn facility and no liquidity runway is computed; the liquidity runway belongs to CP-2D.
No covenant test is applied: the watch levels are not covenant tests; covenant compliance belongs to CP-4.
No maturity or refinancing wall is stressed: debt maturities and refinancing risk belong to CP-2D and CP-3C.

Break points hold cash interest at the base period level (no interest increase). The break at which EBITDA no longer covers cash interest compares same-period flows but is gated like a ratio: it is Not calculable wherever CP-1 has no twelve-month basis for the base period.
A metric that is not calculable under a scenario shows Not calculable against every break point, including a break whose required decline is below that scenario's decline.
Gap (Material): No covenant document or maturity schedule is an input to this stress.
